Set up & run

Setup

Install once per machine, adopt each repository once, and keep the plugin current. Per-host install commands and flags are on Get started; this page does not repeat them.

In plain words

Setup is two separate things. Installing puts Sigma on your computer, once. Adopting a repository tells Sigma to work there: it creates a small .sdlc folder and asks two questions (where your to-do list lives, and which command proves your tests pass). You can re-run adoption any time; it does not ask an answered question again.

1. Install

The commands differ per host (Claude Code and Codex use a plugin marketplace; Cursor and Antigravity run from a clone). They are on Get started, and what was measured on each host is on Hosts.

Needed on the machine: git, bash and python3 (standard library only). The GitHub CLI gh, logged in, is optional: only GitHub issues as the backlog, a Projects board and a pull request per goal need it.

2. Adopt a repository with /sigma-init

Run it from the root of the repository, once, on every host. /sigma-setup is an alias of the same flow.

It doesDetail
Checks accessA git repository, an origin remote, the base branch pushed, gh installed and logged in, and the token's scopes. Each failure prints its own fix; Sigma never runs the interactive login for you.
Asks where goals liveLocal files in .sdlc/goals/, or GitHub issues labelled sdlc:goal. GitHub is the default when origin is a GitHub repository.
Asks for your verify commandIt lists the test commands it detected, each with a number and an id. You confirm one, give your own, or decline. Confirming turns verify.enforce on; declining leaves it off and records why. A literal command typed into the flag is refused on purpose.
Scaffolds .sdlcWrites the config, a project notes file and an example goal, and git-ignores the machine-written folders.
Offers, never forcesA Projects board (--board yes), the team ledger, a product vision (--vision), a runnable demo goal (--demo). With no usable remote it prints a decision and flips nothing; --local-only goes on without a remote.

Right after init, git status shows .gitignore and .sdlc/ as untracked. That is expected. Commit .gitignore and the durable files; what to commit and what to ignore is on The .sdlc folder.

On Codex, Cursor and Antigravity there is no interactive question. The flow prints each open question as an [ask] line with the flag that answers it, and --yes takes the safe defaults: the detected mode, ledger off, and never a board, a verify command or a work flip.

3. Check with /sigma-doctor

Run it after install, after adoption, and whenever something behaves oddly. It checks the project setup, dependencies and host support and prints the fix command beside each problem. It also prints a live dashboard of which optional features are on. If the team ledger is enabled but not set up, it sets it up.

/sigma-status is the lighter check: backlog counts and whether the review queue needs you.

Updating

HostUpdate
Claude Codeclaude plugin update sigmaloop@sigmaloop, then restart the session. Use the full plugin@marketplace id: older releases of Claude Code failed on the bare name.
Codex, Cursor, AntigravityUpdate the plugin or pull the clone you installed from, then start a fresh session.

An update replaces skills, docs, hooks and scripts. It never rewrites your .sdlc/config.json. A block added by a later release does not appear in a repository adopted earlier: copy it from the template in the installed plugin, with every enabled left false, and open one gate at a time. Configuration says what each key does.

If a watcher is running, stop it so the next trigger starts it on the new build: touch .sdlc/state/watch.stop. What each release changes by default is on Releases.

An install under the old plugin id stops updating

Before launch the plugin and marketplace had another id. An install recorded under it keeps working and silently stops receiving updates. /sigma-doctor detects it and prints the commands to switch; it runs none of them. The sequence has not been run against a real pre-launch install.

Technical detail

The init flow is safe to re-run and never changes a setting in .sdlc/config.json unless you pass the flag for it on that run. Verify trust is per checkout and is deliberately not committed: a fresh clone, and every cloud session, must grant it again (or the operator approves the command once in the environment's settings). Without it the verify command is refused and a goal never reaches a pull request. Sources: upgrading, cloud sessions, uninstall.
